Me, Konatsu, Tadayasu and one more, Ritsu Kazama. Those four made up the team. We entered no competitions, but a team is a team.

Ritsu was the same age as the rest of us and lived the loosest life of the four, yet she pushed hard to act like everybody's didi. Maybe to back up that authority, she always arrived at school with time to spare. Then she scolded whoever came after her.

She had come early by her own choice. But if she was left alone too long she got lonely, then angry, and somehow that became our fault.

She could have chatted with her other classmates, of course. Unfortunately, the only students who arrive that early are the model students, and Ritsu was a magnificent anti-model with nothing to say to them.

So the frustration came to us. Mostly to me. Why me? Pata nahin, honestly.

At least, unlike Konatsu, Ritsu did not use violence. She was more civilised. She used words, and I could hear her now as clearly as if she had walked in.

He answered in his usual fluttering voice. Which meant he was serious.

That was the frightening thing about Tadayasu. This part was not a joke. A professional racer has to get through a lot of gates, and he was working honestly toward every one of them.

He never stopped studying or collecting information. He ran every morning for stamina. He never skipped swimming either, which is said to be compulsory for anyone who handles a crucible.

To learn the real technique, he would need to own one. His plan was to earn the money by helping in his father's business for a few years after graduating, so he was studying for that as well.

Crucibles are expensive, naturally. A racing crucible is nothing like a combat tsurugi—those are not even sold on the market—but it is still a rare item. Even an outdated second-hand one would never come in under a million. This was no owning-a-car dream; the price of the dream was in another class.

Tadayasu was lucky. His father was a trading-company man, which counts as elite these days, so a few years of work could cover it. Even so, most people would have said "chhodo yaar" and given up.

How a man this thin and light had grown such a spine was a mystery. Human beings have hidden compartments.

いつも通りピラピラした声で応じる忠保。
　つまりは真剣ということだ。

　そう、冗談ではないところがこの男は凄い。
　プロのレーサーになろうと思えばいくつもの関門を
突破しなくてはならないが、忠保は本気でそのゴール
を目指して努力している。

　常から勉強と情報収集を怠らないのは無論のこと、
体力作りのため毎朝走り込んでいるし、劔冑を扱うの
なら必修といわれる水泳も欠かさない。

　実際の技術を習得するには劔冑を手に入れなくては
ならないが、その資金は学校卒業後に数年間、父親の
仕事を手伝うことでまかなうつもりらしい。
　だからそのための勉強もしている。

　当たり前だが<ruby>劔冑<rt>クルス</rt></ruby>は高価だ。
　本職の武者がよろう戦闘用の<ruby>劔冑<rt>ツルギ</rt></ruby>とは比較にならない
ものの――そもそも市販などされない――、競技用劔冑
とて十分に希少な品である。

　型落ちの中古品でさえ絶対に百万は下るまい。
　マイカードリームとは夢の値段が違う。

　それだけの金額を数年で稼げる見込みのある忠保は
――忠保の父親はいわゆる商社マン、今の世の中では
エリートと言っていい――確かに恵まれている方だが、
それでも普通は諦めてしまうところだ。

　どこをどう見ようと薄くて軽いこの男の人格になぜ
そんな根性があるのか、これはもう神秘である。
　人間は奥が深い。

忠保"And now?"

忠保"You are old before your time, Yuhi."
雄飛"Haan."

鈴川"Thus the Shogunal Administration was dissolved, and the Naifu family's rule over Yamato (the Tokugawa house, as everybody here should know) came to its end in Ten'ei 6—National Year 2517, or 1857 by the Western calendar. From the opening of the government in 2260, the domain era lasted roughly two hundred and fifty years—two hundred and fifty-seven, if one is being pedantic, and in this classroom one is. No other governing system in Yamato's history has lasted so long. I do not say 'almost none.' I say none. Even in world history it is unusual; most systems rot before they gather that much history. Maebashi!"

鈴川"Dhyaan kidhar hai? Why do you think the Tokugawa Administration could rule Yamato for so long?"
ｅｔｃ／前橋"...I don't know, sir."
鈴川"A guess is acceptable. Guess."
ｅｔｃ／前橋"...Because every Naifu lord was, um, very excellent?"
鈴川"Hm. That can be said of some among the fifteen. But take the fifth, Tsunayoshi of the Edicts on Compassion for Living Things. Was he an excellent ruler?"
ｅｔｃ／前橋"No, sir..."
鈴川"As a moralist, perhaps admirable. As a governor, not admirable. Yet the Administration still functioned, more or less properly, under him. Inagi. Why do you think?"

Bossy, playful, sloppy—lekin oddly dutiful. That dutifulness had shown itself as perfect attendance, a record that stopped at yesterday.

Her health was excellent. An elephant could step on her and achieve only moderate success.

Unlike Konatsu and me, standard-issue aam aadmi, Tadayasu came from a family comfortably above middle class. ◆Honestly, why he went to such an ordinary school was a mystery. ◆The information that reached him was far more than what reached us.
